dead-animal-removal.intro: Loris is Horry County's farm town — a small community inland from the Grand Strand, in tobacco-and-timber country where the housing is older farmhouses and in-town homes on generous lots, with barns and outbuildings on most rural parcels. Its dead-animal work is the inland Horry standard: raccoons and opossums dead in crawlspaces and under porches over the winter, found by smell in the spring; animals in the barns and well houses, where a carcass is also a sanitation problem for feed and stock; and wall-void deaths in the older homes, where the scratching stops midweek and the odour starts the following one. In farm country the search area is the whole property, and the removal is only finished when the entry that admitted the animal has been found.
dead-animal-removal.extendedBody:
House, barn, and the space between

A Loris dead-animal call is worked as a property search with priorities: the house first, by evidence — fly activity, vent staining, the household's noise history — with the crawlspace walked completely and the wall voids probed where the sign points. Then the outbuildings, because on a farm parcel the carcass in the barn or the well house is found by the same evidence and matters to the feed and the animals housed there. Removal is sealed, the void treated, and the entry identified: in Loris' older stock it is usually a failed vent screen, a foundation gap at an addition, or a porch void that was never closed — each one quoted for screening while we are on the property. The principle is the county's usual economy: one visit that finds the carcass, closes the door, and surveys the other structures beats three visits that each do a third of it, and on a working farm the survey usually earns its keep in the same hour.

faqs.q: How much does dead animal removal cost in Loris?
faqs.a: It depends on where the animal is and how many structures the search has to cover — a crawlspace carcass in the house is the compact version; a farm parcel where the source has to be found among house, barn, and well house is a longer search. We work by evidence, locate before we price the removal, and quote the entry closing in the same visit. Farm properties get the whole-property read because in Loris the second structure is so often part of the story.

faqs.q: An animal died in our Loris barn near the feed. Is that a health problem for our animals?
faqs.a: It is worth handling promptly and properly. A carcass near feed is a contamination and fly problem first, and the removal includes bagging and taking it away and treating the immediate area — not dragging it to the woodline, which just moves the problem to where the dogs will find it. Tell us on the call that it is a feed-area carcass and we will prioritise accordingly. We will also show you how it got in: barns admit animals through the same gaps year after year, and the screening conversation for a feed room is about your animals' health as much as the wildlife's tenancy.
